discharge_diagnosis: Primary osteoarthritis of right knee, status post right total knee arthroplasty. Uncomplicated hospital course.

discharge_medications.name: oxycodone
discharge_medications.frequency: every 6 hours as needed for severe pain

instructions.wound_care: Keep waterproof dressing on and dry until the 2-week wound check. Do not submerge. A small amount of clear or pink drainage is expected in the first 2-3 days.
instructions.activity: Home exercises 3 times daily. Outpatient physical therapy starts 2026-09-14. Walk short distances every 1-2 hours while awake.
instructions.swelling: Ice 20 minutes at a time, several times a day. Elevate the leg above heart level when resting. Swelling and bruising of the knee, thigh and shin are expected for several weeks.
instructions.diet: Regular diabetic diet. Drink plenty of water.

warning_list: Call 911 for chest pain, trouble breathing, coughing up blood, or if you faint.
Call the on-call line right away for pain, swelling, warmth or tenderness in your calf - this can be a blood clot.
Call for a temperature above 101F (38.3C) or chills.
Call for drainage from the incision that is yellow, green, cloudy, or has a bad smell, or drainage that increases after day 3.
Call for redness that spreads away from the incision, or red streaks.
Call for bleeding that soaks through the dressing. You are on a blood thinner; if bleeding does not stop with 10 minutes of firm pressure, call 911.
Call if your foot or toes become cold, pale, blue, or numb, or you cannot move your foot.
Call if you fall, or your knee suddenly cannot bear weight.
Call if pain is not controlled by your medication as prescribed.
